title: Validate exports before repinning the companion
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate exports before repinning the companion**

When a rebuilt DLL omits `ShowVv5TimeWarp` or another required export, this settlement path repins the DLL, regenerates the dependent artifacts, and ultimately prints `settled` without ever calling `_pe_export_names`, `_certified_vv5_task9_record`, or `load_builds`; the broken artifact is rejected only later when the patcher or tests load the catalog. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier export-surface finding is the newly added settlement script itself, which bypasses the new validator before blessing the DLL, so validate the export table before this swap or run catalog validation before reporting success.

title: Correct the reversed charge-owner contract
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the reversed charge-owner contract**

This newly added contract says the companion deliberately does not charge and that the executable deducts after return, but the code immediately below and `ShowVv5TimeWarp` now do the exact opposite: the companion charges before mutation and the executable never charges. The native function header and generated `upgrade_specs.time_warp.writer` repeat the stale ownership model, so a maintainer following the documented transaction could reintroduce a post-mutation or double charge; update all three descriptions to match the new ordering.

title: Query review summaries before claiming complete coverage
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Query review summaries before claiming complete coverage**

The replacement audit says the earlier failure to query review summaries is fixed, but this GraphQL selection still reads only `reviewThreads` and their inline comments; it never selects `reviews` or `latestReviews`, even though the preceding section identifies those as the sources of review summaries. When a bot finding exists only in a review body, it is absent from the reported 239-thread sweep and cannot have been checked, so add and paginate the reviews connection or narrow the audit's completeness claim.

title: Keep branch-audit coverage proportional to available fixtures
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep branch-audit coverage proportional to available fixtures**

When `va_of` starts returning `None` for most installed branch rows because a section mapping or manifest offset drifts, the loop silently skips those rows and this weakened assertion still passes as long as one branch remains mappable. The former floor was incompatible with partial fixture sets, but replacing it with `> 0` removes the only guard against broad audit coverage loss and can let the same kind of bad native branch this test targets ship unchecked; assert an expected count per available game or fail each installed branch whose source cannot be mapped.

title: Revalidate capacity when the deferred barrel is delivered
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate capacity when the deferred barrel is delivered**

Forcing the random roll to `0x63` requests three children but does not reserve three villager records. Capacity is checked when the player buys the Barrel, while VV1 deliberately waits another 180 update ticks before dispatching it (VV2 waits 90), so if a pregnancy or another event occupies a slot during that interval, the stock per-child allocation can still stop after one or two children despite the full 75,000-point charge. Recheck or reserve all three slots at delivery time before consuming the paid event.
